newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money still stable at 3.05/3.06 pct.
newsitem.headline: German call money still stable at 3.05/3.06 pct.

text.p: German call money rates remained steady at 3.05/3.06 percent in dealings on Wednesday as traders described quiet activity,unchanged from Tuesday.
Dealers showed little reaction to the Bundesbank draining 400 million marks from the market in its weekly repo allocation.
However they said the move was not expected since the market generally expected the central bank to add funds.
"The market is very quiet and the tender had little impact. We had expected an addition of about one to two billion marks but the liquidity situation is sufficient," a trader said.
Daily reserves held by commercial banks at the Bundesbank rose to 42.6 billion marks as of Tuesday, up from 40.7 billion marks on Monday.
The monthly average rose to 40.1 billion marks as of Tuesday compared with 39.9 billion marks on Monday.
Lombard borrowings were about 100 million marks on Tuesday, the same as on Monday.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average on Wednesday stood at 3.08400 percent compared with Tuesday's level of 3.08667 percent.
